subject: Life Skills
title: I-Statements vs You-Statements
description: A 60-second lesson on I-Statements vs You-Statements.

hook.text: 'You never listen to me' triggers defense. 'I feel unheard when I'm interrupted' invites understanding.

buildup.text: You-statements assign blame and put the other person on trial. Their instinct is to defend, not reflect.

discovery.text: I-statements describe your experience without judging theirs: I feel, when, because. Three simple parts.

twist.text: 'I feel that you're wrong' is a disguised you-statement. The word 'that' after 'feel' is usually a trap.

climax.text: Practice the formula: 'I feel [emotion] when [behavior] because [impact].' It stays honest and non-blaming.

punchline.text: Start with I, state the feeling, skip the blame.

quiz.question: What is wrong with saying 'I feel that you're selfish'?
options: It's a disguised you-statement that assigns blame
Feelings should never be shared during conflict
